chicken.substitute: Soy Chunks (Nutrela) or Mushroom or Firm Tofu
chicken.context: For a chewy texture similar to chicken, hydrate soy chunks (Nutrela) in hot water, squeeze dry, and pan-fry. Alternatively, use firm tofu or button mushrooms.

beef.context: Use raw young jackfruit (kathal) for a pulled-meat texture, or soya kheema for minced meat recipes.

mutton.context: Raw jackfruit (kathal) pressure-cooked mimics the fibrous texture of mutton perfectly in Indian curries.

fish.substitute: Mashed raw banana or Tofu with mustard paste
fish.context: Use mashed raw banana (kachha kela) or tofu marinated in mustard seed paste (sarson) to mimic the coastal flavor profile.

egg.context: For binding in baking/fritters, use 1 tbsp ground flaxseed (alsi) mixed with 3 tbsp water. For scrambles (bhurji), use crumbled firm tofu with a pinch of turmeric.

butter.context: Substitute with refined coconut oil for baking, or peanut oil/mustard oil for savory cooking.

ghee.context: Substitute with virgin coconut oil to maintain the rich fat content, or cashew paste for richness in gravies.

paneer.context: Press the tofu for 15 minutes to remove excess water, then pan-fry it lightly to mimic the firm texture of paneer.

milk.context: Use coconut milk for thick curries and desserts (kheer). For a neutral taste, blend soaked cashews with water.

cream.substitute: Cashew Cream (Kaju Paste) or Thick Coconut Milk
cream.context: Soak cashews (kaju) in hot water for 30 mins and blend to a smooth paste to add rich creaminess to curries like Dal Makhani or Shahi gravy.

heavy cream.context: Soak cashews (kaju) in hot water for 30 mins and blend to a smooth paste.

honey.context: Melt jaggery (gud) with a tiny splash of water to mimic the sticky sweetness of honey.

curd.context: For marinades (like tikka), use a thick paste of cashew/peanut with lemon juice and a pinch of amchur (dry mango powder) for tanginess.

yogurt.context: For marinades, use a thick paste of cashew with lemon juice and amchur (dry mango powder).
